content:
Repeating the same action over and over again and expecting different results is the definition of madness.

It seems that is also the message Republicans want to send to voters for the midterms.

Tell me you don't have a midterm message without telling me you don't have a midterm message.

Political analysts point to numbers showing a potential "blue wave" that could return the House to Democrats, fueled in part by Donald Trump's polling hitting historic lows.

Republicans appear destined to lose big in House races unless they can craft a message persuading voters to keep them in power.

House Speaker Mike Johnson had a chance Tuesday to make the case to voters during an appearance on CNBC's "Squawk Box" — and instead did the Democrats a big favor.

"What we're going to do over the next two years is exactly what we've been doing, which is creating the conditions for a strong America," Johnson said.

He elaborated:

Johnson's bid to win hearts and minds with a continuation of the same policies that have led to a war with Iran, higher gas prices and inflation went over about as well as you'd expect.

Indeed, the reaction was the same cold shoulder given to Vice President JD Vance earlier this month when he brazenly asked voters to "give us another chance."
